info.bio: The Dandy Warhols son un grupo de pop rock alternativo, formado en 1993 y procedente de Oregón, Estados Unidos. Estuvieron conformados originalmente por Courtney Taylor-Taylor (voz, guitarra), Zia McCabe (teclado), Peter Holmström (guitarra), y Eric Hedford (batería); hasta que Hedford se retiró del grupo en 1998 y fue reemplazado en la batería por el primo de Taylor-Taylor, Brennt De Boer. Su primer disco "Dandys rules, ok?" fue publicado en 1995

scenes.name: Post-psicodelia (EE UU)
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La psicodelia, el mayor invento de los sesenta, sigue siendo el género dominante en los noventa, con los mismos estilos básicos (el pop psicodélico de los Doors, el freak-out de Red Crayola, el trance de la Velvet, la jam de los Grateful Dead) más el dream-pop y el shoegazing. Mercury Rev logran una síntesis de proporciones históricas (Yerself Is Steam, Deserter's Songs); Luna, Motion Picture, Arson Garden, Tadpoles, Uncle Wiggly, Brother J.T., Space Needle. En la Costa Oeste, Medicine, Sky Cries Mary, Brian Jonestown Massacre (enciclopedias psicodélicas), Quasi, Dandy Warhols.

podcast.title: Implied Similarity to Rolling Stones' "Brown Sugar"
podcast.body: The Dandy Warhols were mentioned in a context of sonic coincidences where "nothing involving" them or The Rolling Stones' "Brown Sugar" led to legal action, suggesting an acknowledged similarity between their work and the Stones' song. "Just as there was nothing involving the Dandy Warholz. The Rolling Stones' Brown Sugar."

podcast.title: Keyboardist's Real Estate Career
podcast.body: While waiting for The Dandy Warhols to reunite, keyboardist Zia McCabe pursued a new career and became a successful real estate agent in Portland, Oregon. "While Dandy Warhol's keyboard is Zia McCabe was waiting for the band to reunite, she reinvented herself as a successful real estate agent in Portland, Oregon."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Similarity to Rolling Stones' "Brown Sugar"
podcast.body: The Dandy Warhols' alt-rock hit "Bohemian Like You" from 2000 was widely noted for its significant melodic and structural similarities to The Rolling Stones' 1971 song "Brown Sugar." "But the fact that it sounded a lot like brown sugar from the Rolling Stones did not escape attention."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Similarity to The Rolling Stones
podcast.body: The Dandy Warhols were mentioned in a context of songs sounding alike, specifically in relation to The Rolling Stones' "Brown Sugar," with the implication that no legal action was taken despite potential similarities. "Just as there was nothing involving the Dandy Warholz. And the Rolling Stones' Brown Sugar."

xref.title: Early Interests and Career
xref.body: Born in France and raised in California, Michael Fitzpatrick initially focused on experimental film despite studying some music. After college, he worked as a recording studio engineer, contributing to albums by artists such as Beck and The Dandy Warhols. "Michael Fitzpatrick was born in France but grew up in California. He studied a little music, but experimental film was really his thing."
